text:
Vegas is 13-6-3 in its tenth season, 29 points, and the underlying numbers are among the best in the West: 55.1% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), a penalty kill that allows just 0.46 expected goals a game, and a 97% playoff chance in our simulations, projected at 104 points.

The engine is the line of Mark Stone, Ivan Barbashev and Jack Eichel, 58% of the chances and 10 goals for against 4, and the pairing of Brayden McNabb and Shea Theodore, 58% and 20-12 in goals. Victor Olofsson has been a revelation in a smaller role, 11 points in 9 games on 5.9 expected, so expect that pace to cool. Adin Hill is hot too, .930 and 5.4 saved above expected over his last five. Rookie Trevor Connelly has scored big goals on the last road trip, and there are calls for a bigger role.

The softer spots are clear. The Nic Dowd, Marc Gatcomb and Braeden Bowman line has 32% of the chances and has been outscored 6-1, and Rasmus Andersson with Jeremy Lauzon sits at 40%. Sunday's 6-3 home loss to a Vancouver team that hadn't won in seven games was ugly, and Stone said as much afterward, telling Jesse Granger of The Athletic, "I don't think we managed momentum very well." Tomas Hertl's hit on Nashville's Mavrik Bourque may also draw a look from Player Safety. One bad night doesn't change what this team is.
